alignments.note: Construct noun of the superscription; the indefinite article belongs to the nominal expression it determines under rule 15 and is not `added`. Head on the lexeme-bearing noun.

Separately segmented determined-state/article morpheme on the rectum. The ASV writes no *the* anywhere in the phrase — the only determiner is the *A* of *A Song*, which rule 15 gives the construct noun — so under rule 29's last sentence the article is unrepresented. No fronting arises, since fronting answers to a phrase whose single written *the* has to be placed.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the noun.
Preposition of authorship rendered *of*; the word states its own relation, so rule 11 places it here.
Proper name.
Presentative particle rendered *Behold*.
Exclamatory interrogative rendered *how*.
Predicate adjective. The clause's one written copula is placed on the second predicate; see that unit's note.
Conjunction rendered *and* under rule 14.
Second exclamatory interrogative, rendered by its own *how*; the ASV writes one for each morpheme, so nothing is distributed here.

Predicate adjective with the construction-supplied copula under rule 20, discontinuous around the expletive under rule 25. The verse writes two coordinated predicates and one *is*; I gave it to the nearer predicate, beside whose rendering the ASV wrote it, as rule 47 reads which word the single written determiner stands beside. The materially different reading puts *is* on `טוֹב` as the first predicate of the pair; nothing else in the alignment changes.

Anticipatory *it* filling the English subject slot for the extraposed infinitival subject the Hebrew writes. Rule 25's closing sentences mark such an expletive `added` while the predicate keeps the copula, exactly as `תוֹעֲבַת כְּסִילִים סוּר מֵרָע` → *it is an abomination ... to depart from evil* does.

Infinitive construct with no preposition on it. English writes no bare infinitive clause with an overt subject, so the *For ... to* frame is what the infinitive itself licenses under rule 52's closing sentences, and neither word is `added`. The unit is discontinuous around the infinitive's own subject noun under rule 25; head on the lexical verb under rule 24. The competing reading gives *For* to `אַחִים` under rule 33, which I set aside because an infinitive's subject is not an adverbial case-function.
Subject of the infinitive construct, rendered by its own noun.
Emphatic particle for which the ASV writes nothing; *together in unity* both realize `יַחַד` (see the next unit), and no English word carries the additive sense of `גַּם`.

The ASV realizes the one adverb/noun `יַחַד` twice, as *together* and again as *in unity*, both writing its lexeme; rule 25 keeps both realizations in that morpheme's one unit, headed on the first occurrence. The competing reading takes *in unity* as an `added` supplied phrase under rule 2; I set it aside because the lexeme `יַחַד` is precisely unitedness, so the words are a doubled rendering rather than English no morpheme owns.

review_notes: Superscription and psalm body are aligned together as one verse, as the packet supplies them.
The single written copula was allocated to the second of two coordinated predicates; the alternative reading is named in that unit's note.

alignments.note: Referential subject *It*, pointing back to the dwelling of the previous verse. No morpheme in this verse answers to it — the clause is verbless with a prepositional predicate — so rule 20's closing sentences and rule 25 mark it `added`; rule 10 makes the verse the whole unit of work, so the antecedent in v.1 does not license it here.

Comparative preposition heading the clause's predicate; the construction-supplied copula joins it under rule 49 and the unit heads on the preposition. MACULA tags the form `Rd`, the article being separately supplied as s002.

Article assimilated into the pointed preposition and supplied by MACULA as a bracketed token; it is a real token and takes the written *the* under rule 12. It is the noun's own article and stands first, so rule 47 gives it the phrase's single *the*.
Head noun of the comparison.
Agreement article on the attributive adjective. The ASV writes one *the* for the phrase, which rule 47 gives to the first article, so this repeated one is unrepresented.
Attributive adjective rendered *precious*; English reorders the determiner ahead of it, which rule 47 anticipates.
Preposition rendered *upon*.
Article with its written *the*.
Noun.

Articleless participle modifying the oil, recast by the ASV as a relative clause; rule 41 keeps the supplied relative with the attributive itself, so *That* is not `added`. None of rule 41's four marks of predication is present — no subject or resumptive pronoun, no coordinated finite clause, no parallel main-clause rendering, and the participle follows rather than precedes its noun. *down* is the phrasal particle completing `יָרַד`'s own lexeme and stays with the verb under rule 44; head on the lexical verb.
Preposition rendered *upon*.
Article with its written *the*.
Noun.

Appositional *Even* before the appositive `זְקַן אַהֲרֹן`. No object marker and no connective morpheme stands on that phrase, so under rule 16 no morpheme licenses the word and it is its own `added` unit; it is not folded into the noun or the name standing beside it.
Construct noun. The ASV recasts the chain's relation as an English possessive on the name, so the construct keeps only its own word under rule 29's possessive case.
Nomen rectum written as an English possessive standing before its head noun; the whole possessive expression is the name's rendering under rule 29.
Written relative morpheme taking the ASV's *That*.
Participle predicating inside the relative clause; *down* is the phrasal particle of the English rendering of `יָרַד` and stays with the verb under rule 44.
Preposition rendered *upon*.

Construct noun rendered *skirt*. No article morpheme stands in the phrase and the rectum carries a possessive suffix, so the *the* is supplied on the construct under rule 29. The margin's *Or, collar* was read and set aside under rule 38: what is aligned is the printed text.
Nomen rectum with the chain's *of* under rule 19, discontinuous around the possessive pronoun under rule 25; head on the noun.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive *his* under rule 18.

review_notes: The clause-initial *It* is `added` and the copula goes to the comparative preposition heading the predicate, per rules 20, 25 and 49.
The ASV marginal note *Or, collar* on `פִּי מִדּוֹתָיו` was read and set aside; the printed *skirt* is what is aligned.

alignments.note: Comparative preposition rendered *Like*. The verse writes no copula here, so nothing of rule 49's frame is to be placed.
Construct noun with a supplied *the* under rule 29, no article morpheme standing in the phrase; head on the noun.
Nomen rectum with the chain's *of* under rule 19.
Written relative morpheme taking the ASV's *That*.
Participle inside the relative clause; *down* completes the English rendering of `יָרַד` as a phrasal verb and stays with it under rule 44, the head remaining on the lexical verb.
Preposition rendered *upon*.
Construct noun with a supplied *the* under rule 29; no article morpheme stands in the chain.
Nomen rectum with the chain's *of* under rule 19.
Causal conjunction rendered *For* under rule 14; a written morpheme answers to the connective, so nothing here is `added`.
Locative adverb rendered *there*.
Finite verb with its own lexical rendering; the explicit subject noun stands as its own unit, so only the verb belongs here.
Explicit subject, the divine name; English fronts it before the verb, which rule 25 allows.

Definite direct-object marker. The ASV writes the object bare — *commanded the blessing* — and spends no word on the object relation, so under rule 16 the marker is its own unrepresented unit. The *Even* standing later in the verse is not this marker's; see that unit's note.
Article with its written *the*.
Object noun.

Appositional *Even* introducing `חַיִּים` as an appositive to *the blessing*. The verse's one object marker stands on `הַבְּרָכָה`, which the ASV renders bare, not on the phrase this word introduces, so rule 16 forbids reaching across the clause for it and the word is its own `added` unit — exactly the division rule 16 makes at EZK.4.5.
Appositive noun rendered *life*.
Extent preposition rendered *for*; the ASV writes a word for the preposition's own relation and another for the noun, so rule 2 splits the pair rather than fusing it under rule 30.
Article on `עוֹלָם`. The ASV writes *for evermore* with no *the*, so the article is unrepresented under rule 29.
Noun rendered *evermore*.

review_notes: The object marker is unrepresented and the appositional *Even* is `added`: the marker stands on `הַבְּרָכָה`, which the ASV renders bare, and not on the appositive the English word introduces.
